clue.text: Tory party accommodation out west

parts.note: CON is the short form for a Conservative, a Tory
a DO is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Conservative gathering is lodged somewhere in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out west' marks the definition as American usage, where a condo is an owned flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A condo, short for condominium, is a privately owned apartment in American English.

clue.text: Dismissed mistakenly he is outwardly worried

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for worried sits on the outside, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: cared, as in was anxious about, means worried

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters of he is are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone sacked in error frets about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' looks like part of the surface's anxious mood but gives a word meaning troubled; 'outwardly' makes it the wrapper. Cashiering is a formal military dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cashiered is to be dismissed in disgrace, especially from the armed forces.

clue.text: Absence of sanctions in these secluded parts

parts.note: NO means none of, an absence of
OKs are approvals, so sanctions as a plural noun gives OKS

explanation.surface: Where no penalties apply, you find tucked-away corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are small sheltered corners or recesses, out of the way.

clue.text: Bridge player may make this bid, generally speaking, holding clubs

definitions.text: Bridge player may make this bid

indicators.note: holding says the phrase for generally speaking keeps another piece inside it

parts.note: overall means on the whole, generally speaking
C is the card-game abbreviation for the clubs suit

explanation.surface: A bridge player bids with clubs in hand, broadly speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge an overcall is a bid made after an opponent has already opened the bidding.

clue.text: Fast-food outlets offering cuts of meat, including joints

indicators.note: including says the cuts of meat take the joints within them

parts.note: chops are cuts of meat such as lamb or pork chops
hips are joints of the body

explanation.surface: Takeaways sell slices of meat, some with bones still in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' points at a butcher's joints of meat but means body joints. A chip shop is a British takeaway selling fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Chip shops are British takeaways selling fried fish, chips and similar quick meals.

clue.text: He made contribution to music — a genius

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gifted composer added to the world of music.
explanation.walkthrough: John Cage was an American experimental composer, best known for 4'33", so 'He made contribution to music' points at him.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer John Cage made a famous, much-debated contribution to twentieth-century music.

clue.text: My arrest is imminent, no doubt about it

explanation.surface: Someone expecting to be caught says so with certainty.
explanation.walkthrough: One reading takes 'bound' as tied up by a captor; the other is the idiom of certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means I am about to be tied up; idiomatically it means I am certain.

clue.text: Sister's about to give birth to a little boy

indicators.note: about says the abbreviation for sister goes round the other piece

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for Sister, as in a nun or nurse
to have a baby is to give birth to it

explanation.surface: A nun's sibling is due to deliver a baby son.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaver is an old informal word for a young lad or youngster.

clue.text: Attack on holy man stifling scream

indicators.note: stifling says the abbreviation for the holy man smothers the next piece inside it

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a holy man
a scream is something hilarious, a laugh

explanation.surface: A saint is assaulted while someone muffles his cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scream' suggests a cry of fear but means a huge joke, a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, overwhelming assault.

clue.text: Helping son with career

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong, to hare

explanation.surface: A boy helps out with his chosen profession.
explanation.definitionFit: A helping is a portion, one person's share.

clue.text: Bathroom cleaner one demonstrates to posh female

parts.note: a shower is someone who shows or demonstrates
GEL is girl as said in an upper-class English accent

explanation.surface: A bathroom product is shown off to an upper-class woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bathroom cleaner' suggests bleach, but it is a product that cleans you.
explanation.definitionFit: Shower gel is a liquid soap used for washing yourself in the bathroom.

clue.text: Having difficulty understanding what's easily absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed says the answer is soaked up inside the words what's easily

explanation.surface: Someone struggles with what ought to be simple to take in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all at sea is to be confused, unable to grasp something.

clue.text: Lack of pressure in test cricket?

indicators.note: lack of says a letter is missing from the word for test

parts.note: to inspect is to examine or test
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: A Test match apparently played without any strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'test cricket' reads as the long form of the sport; a Test is an international cricket match. The question mark flags cricket as an example of an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a chirping, jumping creature, one example of the insect class.

clue.text: Visitor's first to get in ale: a good English drink

indicators.note: to get in says the opening letter goes inside the word for ale

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word Visitor's

explanation.surface: A guest gets first go at an English pub pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water.

clue.text: Listed pate ingredients as items frequently consumed?

indicators.note: ingredients says the letters of listed pate are mixed together into something new

explanation.surface: A recipe lists the components of a pâté as everyday fare.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LISTED PATE are rearranged. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple diet is the food someone eats most regularly.

clue.text: 1'I've to learn manoeuvres for unexpected display

indicators.note: manoeuvres says the letters of the preceding words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone must practise a routine for a surprise show.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's stray 1' before I've is a scanning error. The ten letters of I'VE TO LEARN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation is a surprising disclosure, something suddenly made known.

clue.text: Bully boy is overwhelmed by prison sentence

parts.note: Vic is a boy's name, short for Victor

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the word is is swamped inside the prison sentence

parts.note: time is a prison term, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A lad is weighed down by a stretch in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to victimise them, singling them out for cruel treatment.

clue.text: Danger was oddly absent in city of India

indicators.note: oddly absent says the odd-numbered letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A traveller reports that, oddly, there was no danger in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is a city in Uttar Pradesh, home of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Hear a word designed to make a point

indicators.note: designed says the letters of hear a word are arranged to a new plan

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a word chosen to get an argument across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' doubles as the anagram signal and part of the sense: the thing shaped to make a point.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrowhead is the sharpened tip of an arrow, there to give it a point.

clue.text: Call chap up about lead for Rottweiler dog

indicators.note: about says the reversed pair goes round the next letter
up in a down clue means the words are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
BOD is informal British slang for a chap or person

indicators.note: lead for picks the leading letter of the word Rottweiler

explanation.surface: Phone a man about walking a large guard dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NAME and BOD together to DOBEMAN, which goes 'about' R. 'Rottweiler' looks like the definition but only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dobermann is a German breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Adorn part of ship

explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, as in deck the halls; a deck is a floor level of a ship.

clue.text: Who possibly could give backing to political leader in the wrong?

definitions.text: Who possibly could give backing to political leader in the wrong?

parts.words: Who possibly could give backing to political leader in the wrong?
parts.note: a media adviser who twists events in a politician's favour; Who hints at Doctor Who and backing hints at a turning motion

explanation.surface: Asking who would defend a disgraced leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin doctor is a press adviser who presents news in a light favourable to a politician.

clue.text: One taken on board, namely a new team member

parts.note: a rook is a chess piece, one that can be taken on the board
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, meaning namely

explanation.surface: A recruit joins the side, signed up and taken aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken on board' suggests a new signing; here it is a chess piece captured on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or novice, especially in a sports side.

clue.text: Top cricketer facing several balls

parts.note: a slip is a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper in cricket
an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: The best cricket player faces a run of deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective for the cricketer but is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipover is a sleeveless pullover, a top worn over a shirt.

clue.text: Position one's taken, standing on head for exercise

indicators.note: standing on head in a down clue says the words are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to put something is to position it
one's is read as one is, I plus S, giving IS

explanation.surface: A gymnast takes up a headstand pose as a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing on head' looks like gym talk but turns PUT IS upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is a stomach exercise lifting the upper body from lying flat.

clue.text: Be linked to rumpus involving Conservative speaker

indicators.note: involving says the rumpus wraps round the abbreviation for Conservative

parts.note: a row is a noisy quarrel, a rumpus

explanation.surface: A Tory Speaker gets caught up in a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bercow was Speaker of the UK House of Commons from 2009 to 2019, so 'speaker' is a person, not a loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bercow presided over the Commons as its Speaker for a decade.

clue.text: Farm up north: its produce is cut daily

indicators.note: is cut says the produce loses its final letter

parts.note: a crop is a farm's produce
the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A northern farmer's harvest is mown every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A croft is a small farm in the Scottish Highlands, hence 'up north'. 'daily' reads as an adverb but is a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small tenanted smallholding in Scotland.

clue.text: Mark female removed from garment

indicators.note: removed from says the letter for female is taken out of the garment

parts.note: a scarf is a garment worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A woman takes off a stained item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: King accompanied by slender figure

parts.note: slender means thin
K is the abbreviation for King in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch beside a lean silhouette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like a noun for a body shape but is the verb, as in I figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to reckon or suppose, to hold an opinion.

clue.text: One new piece of furniture is inconvenience

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a commode is a chest of drawers, or a chair hiding a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A brand-new chest of drawers turns out to be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconvenience' is a verb here, and 'is' a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode someone is to put them out or trouble them.

clue.text: Compere with urge to be brief, introducing record

indicators.note: to be brief says the word for urge is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
the last letter of the word for urge is the one dropped
to enter data is to record it

explanation.surface: A host is pushed to keep things short when announcing a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' is a link word placing the shortened urge before the record. 'record' suggests a disc but is the verb meaning to note down.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere is a host who introduces acts, as a presenter does on television.

clue.text: Significant turnaround by day school

indicators.note: turnaround says the pieces are spun round and read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A day school makes a notable U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'day school' looks like one idea but splits into D and ETON, an elite boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Noted means well known or distinguished, worthy of notice.
